description: Nora owns a handwoven rug and is considering an informal swap with a local framer who wants the rug. Nora must decide whether to accept the swap and finalize the exact framing work, while a neighbor and the owner of several prints provide relevant input.

agents.name: Mina
agents.role: Neighbor with Knowledge of a Cash Alternative

shared_context.S1: Nora's handwoven rug is available for an informal sale or trade.
shared_context.S2: Nora wants three art prints framed for display in her apartment.
shared_context.S3: Caleb has expressed interest in acquiring the rug and has discussed a possible exchange.
shared_context.S4: Nora makes the final call on the deal and its terms.
shared_context.S5: As part of their usual planning, Nora asks Caleb, Mina, and Owen for relevant details before settling the arrangement.
shared_context.S6: Nora's usual planning practice is to make the verbal decision after each person has had one chance to state relevant terms; she does not wait for formal written quotes or later outside confirmations.

PF1.text: Caleb's actual swap offer is three custom walnut frames, each sized 24x36 inches, with delivery to Nora by July 12, in exchange for the rug with no cash adjustment.

PF2.text: Mina received a cash offer of $420 from a neighbor who would pick up the rug this Saturday; she has not shared that offer with Nora or Caleb.

PF3.text: Owen's three prints require UV-filtering acrylic rather than ordinary glass, and each frame must include hanging hardware for the prints to be safely displayed.

acceptance_conditions: Nora must accept the barter rather than the cash sale.
The barter must have no cash adjustment.
The settlement must provide exactly three frames made of walnut and sized 24x36 inches.
Caleb must commit to delivering the frames by July 12.
The frames must use UV-filtering acrylic.
Hanging hardware must be included for all three frames.
The settled barter terms must be logged as a trade, swap, barter, or frame-delivery commitment.
The cash alternative must be cited as part of the justification for choosing the barter.

content_checks.C3: decisions['frame_count'] == 3 and decisions['frame_material'] == 'walnut' and decisions['frame_size'] == '24x36 inches'
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['barter_terms', 'trade_terms', 'swap_terms', 'frame_delivery', 'delivery'] for c in commitments) and decisions['deal_type'] in ['trade', 'swap', 'barter'] and decisions['cash_adjustment'] == 0

decisive_facts.why: Caleb's specific offer changes the settlement from an unspecified possible trade to a zero-cash barter for exactly three 24x36-inch walnut frames delivered by July 12.
The concrete $420 Saturday cash alternative gives Nora the exact comparison needed to justify choosing Caleb's barter instead of accepting an ungrounded trade.
Owen's print-specific requirements change the framing terms from ordinary unspecified frames to UV-filtering acrylic with hanging hardware.
